The composite absorber consists of soft magnetic material particles (permalloy or sendust) and polystyrene resin.
The volume mixture ratio of magnetic material was varied from 18 vol% to 75 vol%.
The composites with a low volume mixture ratio of soft magnetic material showed a return loss of less than -20 dB in the frequency range from 1 GHz to 10 GHz.
The values of µ' for composites with a high volume mixture ratio of soft magnetic material were less than unity at frequencies above approximately 6 GHz.
The skin depth of the soft magnetic material particles at frequencies above approximately 5 GHz is less than the radius of the particles.
The magnetic moment generated by the eddy current becomes antiparallel to the incident magnetic field, reducing the value of µ'.
The return loss of the absorber is calculated using the relation R=20log |Γ ∗ |.
The maximum bandwidth of the composite absorber is approximately 16%.
Sendust contains no rare metals and has a smaller mass density compared to permalloy.
The mass density of the composite made of 33 vol% sendust is approximately 1.75.
The thickness of the sample for which the return loss becomes less than -20 dB for the composite made of 33 vol% sendust is approximately 4 mm.
The frequency range in which the composites with a high volume mixture ratio of permalloy show a return loss of less than -20 dB is approximately 8 GHz to 20 GHz.
The study investigates the effect of volume mixture ratio and sample thickness on the absorber's performance.
The composite absorber is suitable for use in practical electromagnetic wave absorbers in the frequency range used for ETC systems or mobile phones.
